newsitem.title: JAPAN: S&P puts five South Korean banks on Credit Watch.
newsitem.headline: S&P puts five South Korean banks on Credit Watch.

text.p: Standard & Poor's Corp said on Wednesday that it had placed five South Korean banks on Credit Watch with negative implications.
The five banks are Hanil Bank, Korea Exchange Bank, Korea First Bank, Korea Long-Term Credit Bank and Shinhan Bank, S&P said in a statement.

S&P said its action reflects the deteriorating asset quality and heightening industry risks faced by Korean banks as defaults continue to emerge among Korea's highly leveraged industrial conglomerates.
It said it is concerned about the potential for spillover of defaults to other sectors of the economy and ultimately to the banking sector.

The overall deterioration in asset quality in Korea has recently been demonstrated by the collapse of the Kia group, S&P said, adding that the five banks are among private-sector creditors to the Kia group with aggregate exposure of about 1.7 trillion Korean won.

While the terms of the Kia group's anti-bankruptcy arrangements with creditors will not be available until the end of July, it is expected that the restructuring cost to the five banks will involve additional financial support and loss of interest income, S&P said.
S&P said it will examine the terms of the restructuring arrangement in light of the current financial situation of each bank involved before taking any rating actions.

While the large industrial conglomerates will likely be able to delay outright bankruptcy with protective anti-bankrupty pacts with Korean banks, the financial performance of the industry groups remain fundamentally weak, S&P said. This could result in higher non-performing loans and further weakening of credit quality among many Korean banks, it said.
